title: Responsive Professional Development: A Facilitation Approach for Teachers’ Development in a Physics Teaching Community of Practice
extended_summary:
This paper examines how a university-school partnership program, IPaSS, supports high school physics teachers’ professional learning through a responsive facilitation approach. The authors ask to what extent teachers’ perceptions align with the program’s design principles and how the program helps teachers move from peripheral participation to core membership in a community of practice.

The intervention is not an AI system; it is a professional development model built around responsiveness, co-design, and ongoing adaptation to teachers’ needs. IPaSS provides teachers with university-level physics curricular materials, peer support, and sustained PD across a school year, including summer workshops and online meetings. The facilitation approach uses daily/pre-session surveys, observations, and discussion to modify upcoming PD activities, reorganize teacher pairings, and create opportunities for teachers to share expertise, mentor one another, and lead sessions.

The study involved 13 of 14 high school physics teachers in the first two cohorts of the Illinois Physics and Secondary Schools partnership, using semi-structured interviews, survey responses, and researcher field notes. Teachers reported strong appreciation for access to materials, practical classroom resources, sustained support, collaboration, and the flexibility to adapt materials at their own pace. The authors conclude that responsive PD can strengthen pedagogical support, confidence, belonging, and leadership development, while also expanding the traditional mentor-novice model by enabling mutual learning across experience levels.

identified_tools.use_case: Not studied in this paper. The paper focuses on a responsive professional development program for high school physics teachers, using interviews, surveys, and observations.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative/mixed-methods case study of teacher professional development, not an empirical evaluation of an AI tool. It provides descriptive evidence about PD design and teacher perceptions, but no AI intervention, comparison group, or causal estimate.
impact_tier_rationale: No AI tool effects are reported, so there is no measurable impact on teacher planning quality, instructional practice, or risks attributable to a generative AI system. The paper is relevant contextually to coaching/feedback in PD, but not to AI efficacy.
